# Cardiovascular disease prevention

This fixture mirrors the structure of the RACGP Red Book chapter on
cardiovascular disease prevention. The wording is paraphrased and
lightly invented for testing only; nothing in this file should be
treated as clinical guidance. Real wording lives in the RACGP PDF
referenced by the production ``CORPUS_SOURCES`` entry.

## Risk assessment

For adults aged 45 to 79 without established cardiovascular disease,
calculate absolute CVD risk every two years using the AusCVDRisk
calculator. For adults of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander
descent, begin risk assessment at age 30. Risk should be communicated
in plain language as the chance of a cardiovascular event over the
next five years.

People with established cardiovascular disease, severe chronic kidney
disease, or familial hypercholesterolaemia are considered at clinically
high risk by default and do not require the calculator.

## Lifestyle interventions

Recommend smoking cessation at every visit for current smokers.
Brief advice combined with pharmacotherapy is more effective than
either alone. Encourage at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity
physical activity per week, distributed across most days. Discuss
dietary patterns aligned with the Mediterranean or DASH approach,
emphasising vegetables, legumes, whole grains, and unsaturated fats.

<!-- page break -->

## Pharmacotherapy

For patients at high absolute CVD risk (>= 10% over five years), offer
a statin at moderate to high intensity in conjunction with blood
pressure-lowering therapy where blood pressure is consistently above
140/90 mmHg. For patients at intermediate risk (5% to <10%), discuss
the trade-offs and shared decision-making is appropriate.

Antiplatelet therapy is not routinely recommended for primary
prevention because the bleeding risk usually offsets the cardiovascular
benefit. Reserve aspirin for secondary prevention and selected high-risk
cases after a documented discussion of risks.

## Follow-up

Reassess absolute risk every two years for low- and intermediate-risk
patients, and every six to twelve months for high-risk patients on
pharmacotherapy. Document the calculated risk score, the recommendation
made, and the patient's preference in the medical record.
